extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, receiving Offices, International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities, and national/regional patent Offices implementing the PCT
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive/procedural requirements for filing, searching, publishing, and processing an international patent application under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT). Covers required contents, formalities, search/examination procedures, time limits, and effects in designated/elected States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain, as specified in this Treaty and the Regulations, a request, a description, one or more claims, one or more drawings (where required), and an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract merely serves the purpose of technical information and cannot be taken into account for any other purpose, particularly not for the purpose of interpreting the scope of the protection sought. (Article 3(2)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, physical requirements, unity, and fees for international application
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall: (i) be in a prescribed language; (ii) comply with the prescribed physical requirements; (iii) comply with the prescribed requirement of unity of invention; (iv) be subject to the payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are preconditions for processing; failure to meet them can affect filing date or lead to invitations to correct or to withdrawal. (Article 3(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request shall contain: (i) a petition to the effect that the international application be processed according to this Treaty; (ii) the designation of the Contracting State(s) where protection is desired; (iii) the name of and other prescribed data concerning the applicant and the agent (if any); (iv) the title of the invention; (v) the name of and other prescribed data concerning the inventor where required by national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every designation is subject to payment of the prescribed fee within the prescribed time limit. Omitting inventor data may have no consequence in some States if national law allows later furnishing. (Article 4(1)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the written-description/enablement standard for the international application. (Article 5)

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim or claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought. Claims shall be clear and concise. They shall be fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be consistent with and supported by the description; clarity and conciseness are expressly required. (Article 6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirement and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings shall be required when they are necessary for the understanding of the invention. Where not necessary, the applicant may include such drawings, and any designated Office may require the applicant file such drawings within the prescribed time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are referred to but not included, receiving Office notifies applicant who may furnish them within prescribed time; otherwise references are considered non-existent. (Article 7; Article 14(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application may contain a declaration claiming the priority of one or more earlier applications filed in or for any country party to the Paris Convention. Conditions and effects are as provided in Article 4 of the Stockholm Act of the Paris Convention, subject to specified national-law variations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a priority claim involves national applications or an international application designating only one State, the national law of that State may govern conditions and effect of the priority claim. (Article 8)

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility to file
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resident or national of a Contracting State may file an international application. The Assembly may allow residents/nationals of Paris Convention countries not party to PCT to file international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concepts of residence and nationality and multi-applicant situations are defined in the Regulations. (Article 9)

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing with prescribed receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be filed with the prescribed receiving Office, which will check and process it as provided in this Treaty and the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office is responsible for initial formalities and for accord of international filing date when requirements are met. (Article 10)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for accord of international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving Office shall accord an international filing date if, at time of receipt: (i) applicant does not obviously lack the right to file there; (ii) application is in the prescribed language; (iii) the application contains at least: (a) an indication that it is intended as an international application, (b) designation of at least one Contracting State, (c) name of the applicant as prescribed, (d) a part that appears to be a description, (e) a part that appears to be a claim or claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are missing, the receiving Office invites correction within prescribed time; upon compliance the filing date may be the date of receipt of correction. Filing date confers effect of a regular national application in each designated State. (Article 11(1)-(4))

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and transmittal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy (home copy) shall be kept by the receiving Office, one (record copy) transmitted to the International Bureau, and one (search copy) transmitted to the competent International Searching Authority. The record copy shall be considered the true copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International application is considered withdrawn if the record copy has not been received by the International Bureau within the prescribed time limit. (Article 12)

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of copies to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Any designated Office may ask the International Bureau to transmit to it a copy of the international application prior to the communication under Article 20; the Bureau shall transmit such copy as soon as possible after the expiration of one year from the priority date. The applicant may also transmit copies to designated Offices at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may opt out of receiving copies; applicants may request transmission by the International Bureau. (Article 13)

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office formal defect checks and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall check whether the international application contains defects: (i) not signed as provided in the Regulations; (ii) does not contain prescribed indications concerning the applicant; (iii) does not contain a title; (iv) does not contain an abstract; (v) does not comply to the extent provided in the Regulations with the prescribed physical requirements. If defects are found, the Office shall invite correction within the prescribed time limit, failing which the application shall be considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpaid fees (prescribed under Article 3(4)(iv) or Article 4(2)) within prescribed time can cause withdrawal or partial withdrawal of designations. (Article 14(1),(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: International search obligation and objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Each international application shall be the subject of international search. The objective of the international search is to discover relevant prior art. International search shall be made on the basis of the claims, with due regard to the description and the drawings (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Searching Authority shall endeavor to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit and shall consult documentation specified in the Regulations. (Article 15)

rubrics_metrics.name: International Searching Authority (ISA) competence and appointment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: International search shall be carried out by an International Searching Authority, which may be either a national Office or an intergovernmental organization. Appointment as an ISA is conditional on consent and an agreement with the International Bureau and on satisfying prescribed requirements (manpower, documentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment terms, extensions, and regulatory oversight by the Assembly are specified; requirements are prescribed in the Regulations. (Article 16)

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA procedure: refusal to search and Unity of invention handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA may declare that no international search will be established if: (i) the application relates to subject matter the ISA is not required to search or decides not to search; or (ii) description/claims/drawings fail to comply with prescribed requirements to such extent that a meaningful search could not be carried out. If ISA considers lack of unity, it shall invite the applicant to pay additional fees and will search the 'main invention' and others only if additional fees are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts are not searched and national law of a designated State treats the ISA invitation as justified, the unsearched parts may be considered withdrawn for effects in that State unless special national fees are paid. (Article 17(2)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: International search report (ISR) timing and transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report shall be established within the prescribed time limit and in the prescribed form and be transmitted as soon as established by the ISA to the applicant and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISR or a declaration that no ISR will be established must be translated as provided in the Regulations; translations prepared by or under IB responsibility. (Article 18)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims after ISR (opportunity to amend)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving the international search report, the applicant is entitled to one opportunity to amend the claims by filing amendments with the International Bureau within the prescribed time limit and may file a brief statement explaining the amendments and any impact on the description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. If national law permits amendments beyond that disclosure, failure to comply with the 'not beyond' rule has no consequence in that State. (Article 19)

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to designated Offices (contents and translations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application, together with the international search report (including any indication referred to in Article 17(2)(b)) or the declaration referred to in Article 17(2)(a), shall be communicated to each designated Office as provided in the Regulations. The communication shall include the translation (as prescribed) of the said report or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims have been amended under Article 19(1), the communication shall contain either full text of claims both as filed and as amended or specify the amendments; copies of documents cited in ISR may be sent on request. (Article 20)

rubrics_metrics.name: International publication timing and content control
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall publish international applications promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the priority date (subject to exceptions). Applicant may request earlier publication. The ISR or relevant declaration shall be published as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No international publication if application is withdrawn before technical preparations completed. The IB may omit expressions/drawings considered contrary to morality or public order or disparaging statements, indicating place and number of words/drawings omitted and furnishing individual copies of passages on request. (Article 21(1)-(6))

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of copy, translation, and national fee to designated Offices (time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a copy of the international application and a translation thereof (as prescribed), and pay the national fee (if any), to each designated Office not later than at the expiration of 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text shows '301 months' (OCR); the Treaty provides a 30-month time limit (noting transitional/incompatibility exceptions). Where ISA declares no ISR, the time limit for these acts is the same. Any national law may fix later time limits. (Article 22)

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of national procedure (stay) and applicant option for earlier processing
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall process or examine the international application prior to the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 22. Notwithstanding this, any designated Office may, on the express request of the applicant, process or examine the international application at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default delay gives applicants time to decide on national prosecution after international phase; applicant can request early national processing. (Article 23)

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of effect in designated States (causes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of the international application (as equivalent to a regular national filing) shall cease in any designated State with same consequences as withdrawal of a national application if: (i) applicant withdraws application or designation of that State; (ii) application is considered withdrawn by virtue of Articles 12(3), 14(1)(b), 14(3)(a), or 14(4), or designation considered withdrawn by virtue of Article 14(3)(b); (iii) applicant fails to perform acts referred to in Article 22 within applicable time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding this, a designated Office may maintain the effect provided for in Article 11(3) even where not required to do so. (Article 24)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review by designated Offices of receiving Office / IB errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office has refused to accord a filing date or declared the application considered withdrawn, or IB has made a finding under Article 12(3), the International Bureau shall, at applicant request, send copies of file documents to any designated Office named. Each designated Office shall, provided national fee and appropriate translation furnished, decide whether the refusal/declaration/finding was justified and may, if it finds an error or omission by the receiving Office or IB, treat the international application as if such error/omission had not occurred (for effects in that State).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be presented within prescribed time limits. (Article 25)

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on content removed from publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application contains expressions or drawings contrary to morality or public order, or disparaging statements as defined in the Regulations, the International Bureau may omit such expressions/drawings/statements from publications, indicating the place and number of words or drawings omitted, and furnishing, upon request, individual copies of the omitted passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives IB discretion to protect public order/morality or remove disparaging content while recording omissions for transparency. (Article 21(6))

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not add new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed under Article 19 shall not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If national law permits amendments beyond original disclosure, failure to comply has no consequence in those States; otherwise adding new matter is prohibited in the international phase. (Article 19(2)-(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search for certain national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If national law permits, an applicant filing a national application or a national Office may request/subject a national application to an 'international-type search' carried out by the ISA that would be competent for an international search for that application, subject to language/format conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national application and translation (if required) shall be presented in the form prescribed for international applications; the ISA will be the one competent for international applications filed with the relevant Office. (Article 15(5))
